title: 2002 AMC 12B Problem 3
statement: For how many positive integers \(n\) is \(n^2-3n+2\) a prime number?

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: more than two, but finitely many

solutions.text:
Factor \(n^2-3n+2=(n-1)(n-2).\) For \(n\ge4\) both factors exceed \(1,\) so the value is composite. Checking \(n=1,2,3\) gives \(0,\) \(0,\) and \(2.\) Only \(n=3\) yields a prime, so there is exactly one such \(n.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: \((n-1)(n-2)\) is a product of two integers; for it to be prime one factor must equal \(1\)
